reading.body:
H.R. 8283, the Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026, is a Republican-carried bill with two Democratic cosponsors and six lobbying filings naming it.

The cosponsor list is 21 Republicans and 2 Democrats, Sydney Kamlager-Dove and Josh Gottheimer. That is a party-line-leaning coalition with a narrow bipartisan edge, which is typical for export-control and national security legislation rather than for domestic tech regulation. The bill's own text is tagged to national security and exports, so the subject is control over model weights and who can move them across borders, not compute siting, data centers, or grid interconnection.

The lobbying record is the more informative half. Five organizations filed: FDD Action with two filings, the Information Technology Industry Council twice under separate firm registrations, the Software and Information Industry Association, and Meta Platforms. The presence of two trade associations and one of the largest model developers means the bill touched commercial interests, not only think-tank advocacy. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, so nothing here says whether these organizations supported or opposed the measure.

What the data does not cover: there are no recorded votes, no committee action, no hearing dates, and no dollar amounts. The latest status date is 2026-04-15, and the only substantive link is to the bill's congress.gov record. The connection to compute and power is indirect at best. Model theft legislation governs the export and protection of trained weights, which sit downstream of the data centers and power contracts that make training runs possible, but this bill does not address either.

summary: H.R. 8283, Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-04-15. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: national security and exports. 6 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
